cases.name: sequence-without-name
cases.description: A sequence with no name cannot be referenced

cases.name: duplicate-sequence-name
cases.config: <tdc><env count="2" seed="s"><sequence name="G"><gen type="text" value="a,b"/></sequence><sequence name="G"><gen type="text" value="a,b"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>x</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: parent-not-declared-first
cases.description: A parent named before it is declared — order decides who can filter whom

cases.name: gen-without-type
cases.description: A <gen> with no type at all

cases.name: unknown-gen-type
cases.description: A generator type that does not exist

cases.name: text-without-value
cases.description: A text generator with nothing to pick from

cases.name: uniq-on-a-computed-sequence
cases.description: uniq= on a sequence whose value is derived, not drawn: it used to be accepted and then silently ignored, so the config claimed a unique column and the data disagreed without a word
cases.config: <tdc><env count="3" seed="s"><sequence name="A"><gen type="number" value="1..9"/></sequence><sequence name="B" uniq="true"><compute><result><concat><field name="A"/><str v="x"/></concat></result></compute></sequence></env><block><line><data>${{B}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: uniq-on-a-conditional-sequence
cases.description: the same for `<gen if=…>` branches: a per-row pick among branches is not a draw from one pool, so there is nothing to draw without replacement
cases.config: <tdc><env count="3" seed="s"><sequence name="A"><gen type="number" value="1..9"/></sequence><sequence name="B" uniq="true"><gen type="text" value="x" if="A == 5"/><gen type="text" value="y"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>${{B}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: compute-beside-a-gen-in-one-sequence
cases.description: Two producers in one <sequence>. It used to be accepted and half of it silently dropped — and the implementations did not agree on which half: the reference kept the <gen>, the four ports kept the <compute>. Same config, different data.

cases.name: uniq-on-a-composed-value-of-two-drawn-parts
cases.description: A composed value joining two drawn parts. One drawn part plus constants is honoured — appending a constant cannot make two draws collide — but two parts have no fixed width, so a unique set of parts is not a unique join: 9+15 and 91+5 are the same three characters.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="4" seed="s"><sequence name="X" uniq="true"><gen type="number" value="1..4"/><gen type="text" value="p,q"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>${{X}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: compound-sequence-inside-a-config-level-uniq
cases.description: A group rearranges whole columns between rows, so every member must own exactly one value. A compound sequence owns a field per <gen name>, and there is no single column to move — the rule is documented, but nothing held the five implementations to it until this case.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="4" seed="c" local="en"><uniq><sequence name="D"><gen name="F" type="text" value="a,b,c,d"/><gen name="L" type="text" value="p,q,r,s"/></sequence><sequence name="R"><gen type="number" value="1..9"/></sequence></uniq></env><block><line><data>${{D.F}} ${{R}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: uniq-group-with-a-single-member
cases.description: A group constrains its members against each other, so one member constrains nothing. It used to be dropped in silence: check reported the config valid and the run drew repeats. A warning, not an error — the config still runs, it just does not do what it was written for.

cases.name: sequential-repeat-is-refused
cases.description: repeat= with order="sequential" — the engines disagree about what it produces, so it is refused rather than answered three ways
cases.config: <tdc><env count="3" seed="s" local="en"><sequence name="A"><gen type="text" value="a,b,c" repeat="3" order="sequential"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>${{A}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: sequential-repeat-on-a-date-is-refused
cases.description: The same refusal on a walked date axis — the rule is about the two attributes, not about one generator type
cases.config: <tdc><env count="3" seed="s" local="en"><sequence name="D"><gen type="date" range="2026-01-01..2026-01-31" order="sequential" repeat="2"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>${{D}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: sequential-without-repeat-is-fine
cases.description: A walked column on its own is unaffected
cases.config: <tdc><env count="3" seed="s" local="en"><sequence name="A"><gen type="text" value="a,b,c" order="sequential"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>${{A}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: repeat-without-sequential-is-fine
cases.description: A repeating column on its own is unaffected
cases.config: <tdc><env count="3" seed="s" local="en"><sequence name="A"><gen type="text" value="a,b,c" repeat="3"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>${{A}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: uniq-drops-the-formatting-layer-so-it-is-refused
cases.description: A draw without replacement produces the column directly and never reaches the pipeline that applies mask=, case=, missing=, repeat=, separator= and anomaly=. Those attributes used to vanish in silence, with `check` calling the config valid — a mask asked for and not applied. Applying them instead would break the promise the other way: a mask maps two distinct draws onto the same characters. So the combination is refused and the attribute is named.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="4" seed="s"><sequence name="X" uniq="true"><gen type="number" value="10..99" mask="x"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>${{X}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: uniq-is-read-case-insensitively-like-every-other-boolean
cases.description: `uniq="True"` must mean what `uniq="true"` means. The reference compared the raw attribute against the lowercase literal while the validator lowercased it first, so a capitalised value passed validation as a uniqueness promise and then did nothing — a column with duplicates that `check` had already called valid. This case pins the two sides together: the capitalised form reaches the same refusal.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="4" seed="s"><sequence name="X" uniq="True"><gen type="number" value="10..99" mask="x"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>${{X}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: if-on-a-gen-inside-a-case-is-refused
cases.description: A <case> body is several parts JOINED into one value, so a condition on one part has no answer to give: if it were false, the part would have to become something, and there is no honest candidate. The branch already carries its own condition. It used to be accepted and ignored, so a <gen if="K == p"> inside a case put its value on EVERY row — including the ones the condition excluded — from a config `check` had called valid. Same reasoning as TDC246 beside it: a flag on one part does not describe the row, and neither does a condition.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="4" seed="s"><sequence name="K"><gen type="text" value="p,q"/></sequence><mix name="M" percent="100"><case><gen if="K == p" type="text" value="ONLY-P"/></case></mix></env><block><line><data>${{M}}</data></line></block></tdc>
